title: Analysis record
description:
What one analysis of one request produced that is not a construct: the request it answers, the outcome it reached, the questions it refused to decide, and what it deliberately left out. The named producer is domain-modeler; the named consumers are the impact analysis and the ingestion. This artifact carries control flow — a consumer reads `state` to decide whether there is anything to act on — so it is a versioned schema validated at the boundary rather than prose.

The constructs are absent by design. Each is a file in the knowledge base, addressable by an identifier this record can name, and holding them here as well would put one fact in two places with nothing keeping them in step. What is left is exactly what has no file: a request is not a construct, an exclusion is the absence of one, and an open question bears on several at once.

contract_version.description: The contract this instance declares. A consumer selects behaviour on this value and never infers a version from shape.

record_id.description: Stable identifier for this analysis, required for traceability. The caller supplies it: a producer that minted its own could not have its run repeated and compared.

producer.description: What performed the analysis. Not a const: unlike a result contract owned by one named agent, an analysis is the artifact that matters rather than a particular producer of it.

consumer.description: Who reads it. The impact analysis reads what the run touched; the ingestion reads what it still owes. Neither reads the constructs, which are files.

request.description: What was analysed. It travels with the model because a design decision is only reviewable against the request that prompted it, and because knowledge authored downstream records where it came from.

id.description: The request this analysis answers. A request is prose a person supplied plus the material it names; no capability produces one, so the identifier is the caller's to supply and is never minted here.

description.description: What was asked, in one paragraph a reviewer can check the model against.

artifacts.description: Each artifact the request was read from, by path or stable reference. Non-empty: an analysis whose source cannot be named cannot be reviewed, because nothing states what would have to be re-read to check it.

state.description: The closed outcome a consumer branches on. `analysed` means the run reached a design and wrote it, including where parts of it are recorded as open questions. `blocked` means no analysis was possible at all — the request describes no domain, or is unintelligible — and is a finished run with a negative result rather than an error.

blocking_reason.description: Why no analysis was possible. Required on `blocked` and forbidden otherwise: a blocking reason on a successful result says two things at once.

open_questions.description: What the analysis refused to decide. Held once here and pointed at from every object it blocks, through the gap that names it: a question bearing on four constructs restated four times is four statements that drift.

excluded.description: What the analysis considered and left out, with the reason. It has no file because it is not a construct: absence cannot be inferred from silence, and a reader who finds no mention of persistence cannot otherwise tell whether it was excluded or forgotten.

notes.description: What a reviewer needs that no field above carries. Prose, and nothing branches on it.

written.description: Every object this run wrote, by identifier. The objects themselves are files and are not repeated here — what this answers is which of them this run is responsible for, so a reviewer reading a diff can tell a construct this analysis produced from one that was already there. Empty is legitimate: a run whose every construct was refused wrote nothing and still reached an outcome.

then.description: A blocked run reached no design, so it wrote nothing. Saying both is not redundancy: `state` is what a consumer branches on and `written` is what a reviewer checks the tree against.

else.description: A blocking reason on a run that produced something says two things at once.

then.description: An analysis recording neither an open question nor an exclusion is treated as unreviewed rather than as complete: every request leaves something undecided or something out, and a record showing neither has not been read against the request.

id.description: Derived from the question rather than allocated, like every other identifier in this model: `oq_` followed by the question's subject in snake_case. It exists so a gap on an authored object can name the question that blocks it instead of restating it. In the reference run nine of twelve questions bore on more than one construct, and a question copied into every file it blocks is a question that drifts between them.

question.description: What the request does not answer, phrased so someone who knows the domain can answer it in a sentence.

why_it_matters.description: What the answer would change in the model. A question with no consequence is noise, and one whose consequence is unstated cannot be prioritized.

blocks.description: The objects this question blocks, by identifier. Each carries a gap naming the question, so the two records agree without either restating the other.

reason.description: Why it is out. The two ordinary answers are that it is stack knowledge the knowledge base excludes, and that the request does not reach it.
